source_read: PDF pp. 950-951 (PDFs/MDMA/Nutt_2021_PuttingMDBackIntoMDMA.pdf): the News & Views read in full (standfirst, 11 running-text paragraphs, Fig. 1 and legend, 12 references, affiliations, competing interests); both pages rendered at 110 dpi to fix columns and paragraph breaks; the unrelated piece at the top of p. 950 not used. Authors of references 4, 8 and 10 checked in the Crossref records (api.crossref.org) in my own browser tab. Step 1 (blind extraction) not run this round, per the round brief.

design.note: A News & Views commentary with no data; the schema has no commentary value, so narrative-review with the design_detail saying what it is, is the workable choice. Paragraph count (11; 1-2 begin on p. 950, 3-11 on p. 951) confirmed on the rendered pages.

instrument.note: none-applicable with the editors' narrative-review checklist (METHODS 5.3).

key_findings.note: p. 950: the standfirst says only 'may be a promising treatment'; the 1st paragraph begins in the left column and the efficacy, safety and approval sentences are in its middle-column part. No trial number anywhere in the piece.
p. 950, 1st paragraph, left column; no citation.

The 2nd paragraph runs from the middle column of p. 950 through the right column and ends at the top of the left column of p. 951; the 3rd and 4th paragraphs follow in that column. Merck 1912 (ref 2), 1927 and 1959, Shulgin in the 1970s, couples counselling, raves, the DEA in 1985, MAPS in 1986 and the end-of-1980s bans are all there.
The 5th paragraph begins at the foot of the left column of p. 951 and continues in the middle column.
p. 951, 6th paragraph, middle column. See 'missed': ref 4, the open alcohol-use-disorder trial, has Nutt as last author.
The source says two or three doses a few weeks apart in a structured psychotherapy programme, as the card's exposure field records.

key_findings.correction: Proposed psychotherapeutic mechanism: MDMA facilitates exposure therapy, whose aim is to reactivate and then extinguish the emotional memory of the trauma (ref 7; Fig. 1, whose legend says MDMA treatment facilitates the extinction of these emotional resurgences); in healthy volunteers it reduces the impact of negative memories (refs 8, 9), and human neuroimaging, which the authors call a plausible mechanism, shows it suppressing amygdala responses to negative stimuli (refs 9, 10); it also enhances social connection (refs 11, 12).
key_findings.note: The source does not say that MDMA helps reactivate the memory: the reactivate-then-extinguish aim is ascribed to current treatments, and Fig. 1's legend credits MDMA with facilitating extinction. Locator right (9th paragraph, middle column continued at the top of the right column).
The 11th paragraph opens by saying MDMA treatment gives hope to a field with historically poor outcomes, then makes the rescheduling call.

reporting_issues.note: Searched both pages: no sample size, outcome measure, effect size, interval, rate or adverse-event count; no mention of placebo, blinding or expectancy.

Slightly qualified: the piece calls the phase 2 work MAPS research and the Breakthrough designation one given to 'the MAPS program', and puts the EMA-approved parallel phase 3 design in the same sequence, but it never names the phase 3 sponsor. The link is by implication; the sponsorship itself is stated in the trial report. The consequence stands.

The two commentaries may be naming different steps (criminalization in one, Schedule I classification in the other); neither cites a document, so the section 13 sources should decide, as the card says.

risk_of_bias.note: I agree with the overall judgment (high) and four of the five domains; I would rate 'reliance on the authors' own studies' high, not low (below). The overall does not move.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: Crossref shows Nutt as last author of ref 4 (Sessa et al., J Psychopharmacol 2021, 35(4):375-383, doi 10.1177/0269881121991792), ref 8 (Carhart-Harris et al., Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 2014, 17(4):527-540, doi 10.1017/s1461145713001405) and ref 10 (Carhart-Harris et al., Biol Psychiatry 2015, 78(8):554-562, doi 10.1016/j.biopsych.2013.12.015); with de Wit's refs 9 and 12, 5 of the 12 references are the authors' own. They are not used only for mechanism: ref 4 is the sole evidence for the alcohol-use-disorder efficacy statement and for the forecast of approval in that indication, and refs 9 and 10 are the whole of the human-neuroimaging 'plausible mechanism'. If the editor reads the domain as concerning clinical claims only, some-concerns is the floor.

domains.domain: Balance of evidence on the efficacy and safety of MDMA-assisted therapy

overall.note: High; never less severe than the worst domain.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. One addition: the piece's 'excellent safety profile' goes beyond the trial's own abstract, which says safe and well-tolerated (MAPP1 abstract, read on the publisher's page for this check), and its claim of markedly reduced drinking rests on a study whose own title (Crossref) calls it a first study of safety and tolerability. 'By August 2024 the FDA had rejected the application (Mahase, 2024)' is supportable from the BMJ article's 13 August 2024 date.

missed: Authors' own work, now checkable: refs 4, 8 and 10 have Nutt as last author (Crossref), so with refs 9 and 12 (de Wit) 5 of 12 references are the authors' own. The affiliations_note's statement that further overlap 'cannot be checked' from the list should be replaced by these facts, and the risk-of-bias domain revised (above).

Ref 4 (Sessa et al., 2021), cited for 'remarkably reduced drinking over 9 months' in an open trial in alcohol use disorder, is titled in Crossref as a first study of safety and tolerability; the commentary turns an open-label tolerability study with the first author as last author into evidence of efficacy and a basis for forecasting approval, without saying it is his. Worth a reporting issue.

Reference-list errors (a reporting issue of the kind recorded for Earleywine): ref 8 prints volume 1 and year 2013 for Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 17(4):527-540 (print April 2014, online December 2013); ref 10 prints 2014 for Biol Psychiatry 78(8):554-562 (print October 2015).
Unreferenced statements besides those the card lists: the Breakthrough Therapy designation and the EMA's approval of the protocol design for parallel phase 3 studies (p. 951, 5th paragraph).
